content.text:
{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The entry's core identification—that sapphire is the clear sapphire likeness at God's throne, functioning as the full moon in its enthroned and bridal form, a worn (not owned) brightness whose tohar can cease, and identified with Issachar—best unifies the supplied texts. Exodus 24:10 and Ezekiel 1:26/10:1 fix the sapphire-throne/pavement link with explicit clearness (tohar) compared to heaven; Psalm 89:36-37,44 pairs the enduring throne with the moon as faithful witness and then applies the identical tohar-root to glory that can be made to cease; Song 6:10 and the pearl/bride chain supply the full-moon bridal form; Isaiah 54 and Revelation 21 place sapphire in bridal/foundation settings; the breastplate listing supplies the Issachar identification. The common heaven/throne reading is absorbed rather than contradicted, and no rival accounts for the tohar-glory cessation, moon-throne pairing, and bridal full-moon form with equal textual economy.",
  "book_core_identification": "Sapphire is the clear sapphire likeness at the place of God's throne, identified as the full moon in its enthroned and bridal form—a brightness worn, not owned—whose rare clearness (tohar, Ex 24:10) is the same word for the throne-glory that can be made to cease (Ps 89:44), and is identified with Issachar.",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "The clearness (tohar) of the sapphire pavement is the very word for the throne-glory that can be made to cease (Ps 89:44).",
    "That brightness is worn, not owned.",
    "Sapphire is identified with Issachar."
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Extended calendar/moedim claims (month beginning at full moon, east-gate entry, trampling of times) go beyond the glossary entry.",
    "Detailed unpointed-letter hearings equating keseh/kisse and full pearl-gate typology are chapter developments not required by the printed entry.",
    "Broader merchant/pearl purchase narrative and counterfeit dark-moon polemic exceed the entry's scope."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Sapphire primarily and simply symbolizes the heavenly realm, divine throne, and glory of God (deep-blue pavement/throne appearance in theophany texts), with secondary uses as a precious foundation or breastplate stone; any lunar, bridal, or tohar-cessation reading is later elaboration not required by the plain texts.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Sapphire = heavenly throne/glory/presence of God (theophany stone).",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "SAME_CORE_BROADER",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter does not deny the throne/heaven referent but treats the full-moon enthroned/bridal specification, the worn-not-owned tohar mechanics, and the Issachar link as unnecessary additions rather than the precise identity the texts support.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Ex 24:10 and Ezek 1:26/10:1 directly describe sapphire as pavement under God's feet or likeness of the throne, compared to the body of heaven—sufficient for a heaven/throne symbol without lunar specification.",
    "Rev 21:19 and Isa 54:11 place sapphire among foundation stones of the restored/holy city, a preciousness motif rather than a phase-of-the-moon claim.",
    "Ex 28:18 simply lists sapphire on the breastplate; tribal assignments are variable and secondary.",
    "Color and clarity associations with purity or contemplation are common later readings but not demanded by the Hebrew narratives."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Unifies the identical tohar root across Ex 24:10 (sapphire clearness) and Ps 89:44 (glory/throne that ceases), explaining why the brightness is 'worn, not owned'.",
    "Accounts for Ps 89:36-37's explicit pairing of throne-as-sun and established-as-moon immediately before the tohar-cessation verse.",
    "Integrates Song 6:10 (fair as the moon) and the bridal foundations (Isa 54; Rev 21:9,19,21) into one enthroned-bridal full-moon figure rather than leaving them as disconnected precious-stone catalogs.",
    "Supplies a concrete celestial referent (full moon) that matches the 'body of heaven in his clearness' and the mirror/sky language of Job 37:18,21.",
    "Preserves the common throne/heaven core while tightening it with the supplied cross-text mechanics."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Stays closer to the surface reading of the three primary theophany verses without requiring lunar or bridal typology.",
    "Avoids dependence on unpointed-letter or lexical-range arguments for keseh/tohar.",
    "Matches the broad traditional consensus reported in the common-interpretation responses."
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Exodus 24:10 (sapphire pavement + tohar/clearness = body of heaven)",
    "Psalm 89:36-37,44 (throne as sun/moon; same tohar-root glory made to cease)",
    "Ezekiel 1:26; 10:1 (sapphire likeness of the throne above the firmament)",
    "Song 6:10; Isaiah 54:5,11; Revelation 21:9,19,21 (bridal full-moon and sapphire foundations)",
    "Job 37:18,21 (sky as molten looking-glass cleansed to bright light)"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [
    "The precise breastplate-to-Issachar mapping is traditional/variable and not uniquely proven by the printed references alone.",
    "Whether every reader must hear the full-moon phase rather than a more generic heavenly brightness remains underdetermined by any single verse."
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
